newsitem.title: UK: Pace cautious on first half of year.
newsitem.headline: Pace cautious on first half of year.

text.p: Britain's Pace Micro Technology Plc warned on Wednesday that although it still expected growth in the digital market, amid a realignment of broadcaster ownership, it remained cautious about prospects for the first half of this year.

The satellite and cable television equipment company, which earlier reported flat year pre-tax profits of 18.4 million pounds compared to 18.2 million last time, said it was disappointed that the digital broadcasting market had not grown as rapidly as expected.

Pace, which issued a profit warning in February, blamed recent changes in the ownership of broadcast services, particularly in the U.S., Germany and Italy, for leading to short-term uncertainty in market demand.
Sales in the second half of the year had fallen compared to the first because of a decline in analogue sales -- which was not compensated for by growth in digital sales.
Customers were holding out for the launch of digital services and slow sales were exacerbated by a combination of currency and pricing pressures in continental Europe, the group said.

Analogue sales in the second half fell to 32 million stg from 53 million in the first and digital sales grew less than expected -- with 70 million stg in the second half compared with 65 million in the first.
Pace is one of Europe's leading manufacturers of satellite television receivers and set-top box decoders.
Its shares collapsed this year on doubts over whether it would be awarded a lucrative world-wide contract from British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc as it rolls out its digital satellite TV network.

Pace subsequently won the order along with three other manufacturers, but a public boardroom rift during which one of two chief executives, Barry Rubery, left the company in February amid "irreconcilable differences in management style" has dogged the group.
The group, which has also announced that finance director Steven Jones will leave after a successor is appointed, said it was actively seeking a new chief executive.

In the meantime, chairman Peter Morgan has been working alongside joint chief executive David Hood as joint chief executive. After a successor for Rubery is found, Hood will remain an executive director with ongoing technology brief.
Pace's shares have fallen to an all-time low of 52p from a high of 241p. They were trading at 55p, a loss of eight pence, by 0715 GMT.
